prompt:
**(a)** Let $q(x)=\dfrac{4x^3-6x+\sqrt{x}}{x^2}$. Rewrite $q$ as a sum of power functions, then find $q'(x)$. Do not use the quotient rule.

**(b)** Find an equation of the tangent line, and an equation of the normal line, to the graph of $g(x)=2x^2-8x+5$ at the point $(3,-1)$.

**(c)** Find all points on the graph of $p(x)=x^3-3x^2-9x+4$ at which the tangent line is horizontal.

**(d)** Use the limit definition of the derivative to find $s'(t)$ for $s(t)=80t-5t^2$. Show each step of your work.

rubric.description: (b) Uses slope $-\frac14$ for the normal line: $y+1=-\frac14(x-3)$
(d) Simplifies to $80-10t-5h$ and takes the limit to get $80-10t$

prompt:
Let $f(x)=\begin{cases}x^2-4x+7 & x<3\\ 2x-2 & x\ge3\end{cases}$.

**(a)** Show that $f$ is continuous at $x=3$.

**(b)** Find $\lim_{x\to3^-}f'(x)$ and $\lim_{x\to3^+}f'(x)$.

**(c)** Is $f$ differentiable at $x=3$? Justify your answer using one-sided derivatives, and give an equation for the tangent line at $x=3$ if it exists.

**(d)** Let $g(x)=\begin{cases}x^2-4x+7 & x<3\\ mx+n & x\ge3\end{cases}$. Find the values of $m$ and $n$ for which $g$ is differentiable at $x=3$.

rubric.description: (a) Shows the left limit, right limit and $f(3)$ all equal 4
(b) Finds $f'(x)=2x-4$ for $x<3$ and $f'(x)=2$ for $x>3$, with both one-sided limits equal to 2
(c) Concludes $f$ is differentiable at 3 because it is continuous and the one-sided derivatives agree ($f'(3)=2$)
(c) Gives the tangent line $y-4=2(x-3)$, that is $y=2x-2$

sampleResponse:
(a) $\lim_{x\to3^-}f(x)=9-12+7=4$, $\lim_{x\to3^+}f(x)=6-2=4$ and $f(3)=2(3)-2=4$. All equal, so $f$ is continuous at 3.
(b) For $x<3$, $f'(x)=2x-4\to2$. For $x>3$, $f'(x)=2$. Both one-sided limits are 2.
(c) $f$ is continuous at 3 and the left and right derivatives are both 2, so $f$ is differentiable at 3 with $f'(3)=2$. Tangent line: $y-4=2(x-3)$, i.e. $y=2x-2$.
(d) The slope must match the left piece: $m=2(3)-4=2$. The pieces must meet: $3m+n=4$, so $n=4-6=-2$.
